BACKGROUND. This repo produces a two-person video podcast. Each episode starts as four separate WebM files from a Daily.co room (host camera audio, host camera video, guest camera audio, guest camera video). They do not share a zero: in the reference episode the host tracks start at 0.225s and the guest tracks at 224.875s because the guest joined 224.7 seconds late. Tracks also contain dropouts, meaning stretches where packets stopped arriving.

FIVE CONSECUTIVE RENDERS OF ONE EPISODE SHIPPED BROKEN, all of them audio: (a) the renderer certified the CONTAINER duration instead of counting decoded audio samples; (b) an ffmpeg -shortest flag truncated the AAC tail; (c) a constant-frame-rate clean INSERTED samples because per-contribution timestamps were not rebuilt; (d) gates judged audio/video divergence without first locating the A/V anchors; (e) dropouts were DELETED rather than held, sliding all later audio 77 seconds early. All five are now fixed in the code.

A review established that the QUALITY GATES would not have caught a single one of the five, and that eight separate paths can report success without measuring anything. That is what this work fixes. The ratified rule is: no stage may remove time from one track without removing it from all four, and a gate that cannot fail is not a gate.

YOUR TASK: close the false-green paths that live inside server/pipeline/media_gates.py. A named review found these, each cited to a line you should read before changing it.

1. validate_raw_source_integrity computes the packet-PTS-versus-decoded-duration divergence and then records it with divergence_enforced set to False (near media_gates.py:225). That measurement is exactly what detects defect (e), dropouts being deleted. Make it enforced, with a documented tolerance, and make the tolerance configurable rather than magic.
2. The same validator narrows its input set: _paths (near media_gates.py:56) silently discards None and non-path values, and the gate then requires only ONE surviving track. For a two-person interview it can therefore pass having measured a single stream out of four. Require the full expected set when the caller declares one, and fail loudly naming which tracks were missing.
3. validate_angle_segments (near media_gates.py:377) treats equal stream counts as acceptable, so two adjacent segments that both have zero audio streams pass the audio continuity test without any packet-bound comparison being run. A boundary with no audio to compare is UNMEASURED, not passed.
4. validate_bumpers (near media_gates.py:1512) normalizes through _paths and then requires only that at least one path survive, so a missing intro or outro becomes a one-bumper pass. When the caller supplies both, require both.

Do not change any function signature that orchestrator.py calls. Add optional keyword arguments with defaults if you need new inputs. Another worker is editing orchestrator.py in parallel and you must not break its call sites.

THE RED REQUIREMENT, which is the whole point of this task. Every check you add must be PROVEN CAPABLE OF FAILING. For each one, write a test that feeds a poisoned or missing input and asserts the gate BLOCKS. A test that only proves the happy path passes is worthless here, because passing-without-measuring is precisely the defect class being removed. In your summary, list each new check and the exact poisoned input that makes it fail.

YOUR TASK: connect two finished safety mechanisms that exist and are never called in production, and stop two paths from recording a pass when nothing was measured.

1. av_sync.verify_sync (av_sync.py:93) is a deterministic gate written to catch sync offsets collapsing to zero, which is the historical failure where a guest who joined four minutes late gets treated as present from the start. A repo-wide search finds it only in a shadow script and in tests. Call it in the orchestrator immediately after each offsets_for_paths derivation (near orchestrator.py:2644 and orchestrator.py:3299), record the result as a media gate, and HALT on failure. Read how the existing gates are recorded and halted and follow that same pattern exactly.
2. media_gates.validate_raw_tracks (media_gates.py:83) compares decoded duration against packet PTS span with a percentage tolerance. It is called only by a standalone script. Wire it into the post-download path alongside the raw-integrity gate that already runs there (near orchestrator.py:3237), record it, and halt on failure.
3. _not_applicable_gate (orchestrator.py:151) returns passed True. One of its callers fires when the angle renderer did not expose segment outputs, which is a MISSING MEASUREMENT being recorded as a pass. Separate genuinely-inapplicable (there were no bumpers to check) from not-measured (the thing that should have been measured was absent). Not-measured must not report passed True.
4. _load_true_boundaries (orchestrator.py:164) returns an empty list on OSError or JSON ValueError, and the render then composes a fallback time map from PLANNED values instead of observed encoded boundaries. A passing transfer gate can therefore rest on numbers we hoped for rather than measured. Mark that case unmeasured instead of silently substituting.

Do not edit media_gates.py or av_sync.py; other workers own those files in parallel. Call their existing public functions as they are today.

YOUR TASK: stop a failed media probe from silently producing a plausible wrong answer.

probe_start_time (av_sync.py:190) catches CalledProcessError, ValueError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError and JSONDecodeError, and returns 0.0. Both production callers go through it. If it degrades for the guest's tracks, compute_offsets collapses the roughly 225 second join stagger to zero and the pipeline proceeds confidently with a wrong layout. The module's own docstring names this as the historical bug class.

Make it fail closed: raise a specific, named exception carrying the path and the underlying cause. The orchestrator already wraps both call sites in a broad exception handler that halts and records a media failure, so raising is the correct behavior and does not need an orchestrator change. Update every test in tests/test_av_sync.py that depends on the old return-zero behavior.

YOUR TASK: stop promotional clips being cut on the wrong clock. This is a live bug today, independent of everything else in this batch.

clip_selector reads start and end seconds from transcript.json and passes them UNCHANGED to ffmpeg as seek positions into composite.mp4 (see clip_selector.py:212, :341 and :514). That is an implicit assertion that the transcript and the composite share a zero. They do not. The transcript builds its own origin by parsing a 13-digit epoch out of the source file name, while the composite runs on the raw container clock. On the reference episode those differ, and a cross-correlation measurement of the composite against the master grid found a constant 225.0 millisecond offset at nine probe points spanning 47 minutes.

Make the conversion explicit rather than assumed. Introduce a single, named, tested translation from transcript time to composite time, route every seek through it, and make the module REFUSE to cut when the offset it needs is unknown rather than defaulting to zero. Defaulting to zero is what it does today and is the bug.

Do not edit orchestrator.py, media_gates.py, av_sync.py or promo_clips.py; other workers own some of those in parallel and promo_clips is out of scope for this batch.
